messages:
alex: quick heads-up — saw a customer report where a streaming reconnect after a toolcall TTL trim led to a measurable double-charge. filing here before i open a PagerDuty.
priya: can you paste the minimal repro/logs? wondering if this is router-based or ledger-stitching.
alex: paste of the core timeline (sanitized):
```
[11:02:11] session_id=abc123 start stream -> tokens emited: 95 (prefix A)
[11:02:13] toolcall invoked (TTL=2s) -> router pauses stream, issues TOOLCALL-REQ
[11:02:15] client reconnects (short network blip), new session_id=abc123-1 resume -> stream resumes, server replays prefix A -> tokens emited: 95 (duplicate)
[11:02:16] billing: STREAM_CONFIRMED session=abc123 tokens=95
[11:02:17] billing: TOOLCALL_CONFIRMED session=abc123 tokens=20
[11:02:18] billing: STREAM_CONFIRMED session=abc123-1 tokens=95
```
Result: customer billed for 95+20+95 instead of 95+20 (duplicate 95).
Note: router logs show we did a resume rather than a handoff; stitch info absent.

josh: ouch. This looks like two independent stream-confirmed events because session id mutated on reconnect. Do we currently dedupe by prefix hash anywhere? or only by session id?
maya: we have a prefix hash in the runtime for caching, but billing pipeline dedupe expects a single canonical session token. reconnections that allocate a new session id bypass that check.

priya: billing-bot — can you show how the ledger sees provisional vs confirmed for these events? is there an intermediate provisional entry for the first stream?
billing-bot: Sure — sample ledger trace:
- provisional: STREAM session=abc123 provisional_tokens=95 epoch=1678
- confirmed: TOOLCALL session=abc123 confirmed_tokens=20 epoch=1680
- confirmed: STREAM session=abc123-1 confirmed_tokens=95 epoch=1682
No automatic merge was performed because session ids differ and no stitch tag present.

alex: so root cause = reconnect allocates new session id + no stitching metadata carried over, billing confirms both. the toolcall TTL/unblock window makes this common for mobile clients.
josh: proposed fix: attach a client-stitch-id in the stream handshake (client provided idempotency token) that survives lightweight reconnects. billing pipeline can dedupe confirmed streams that share the same stitch-id and overlapping prefix hash within a short window (e.g., 5s).

maya: UX wise — Console should surface these as "stitchable duplicates" under the session timeline and give ops a button to merge/adjust charges for edge cases while we roll out automatic stitching. maybe show a small warning next to quotas: "possible duplicate tokens from reconnects" with an example link.
priya: agree. also need to consider quota enforcement: if we dedupe after the fact, we mustn't retroactively change quota usage that triggered rate limits. i think policy: dedupe in billing but *don't* roll back quota consumption for enforcement — instead surface a refund workflow.
alex: implementation plan:
- short term: add console flag to mark suspect sessions (match on prefix-hash + near-timestamp). UI: show both sessions linked and checkbox to open a ticket/refund.
- mid term: runtime + router: propagate X-Stitch-Id on handshake when client SDK sets it. server retains stitch-id until TTL.
- long term: billing pipeline: stitch confirmed stream events if stitch-id matches and prefix overlap > 70% within STITCH_WINDOW=5s. add metrics for false merges.

josh: sample handshake snippet (pseudo):
```
client->runtime: STREAM_START { client_id: "u-42", stitch_id: "st-99" }
runtime->router: attach { session_id: uuid(), stitch_id: "st-99" }
on reconnect: client->runtime: STREAM_RESUME { session_hint: previous_session_uuid, stitch_id: "st-99" }
```

maya: question: do we have any security/privacy concerns about client-provided stitch ids? guessing not if they are random GUIDs and we rate-limit them.
priya: also need to update audit logs so any automated stitch can be traced; compliance will want proof.

alex: quick metrics ask — eng-platform: can we add a dashboard panel showing: ratio of duplicate-stream-confirmations (confirmed events with >50% prefix overlap within 10s across sessions) and sum of tokens involved? that will help prioritize.
josh: i'll prototype a query against the event-store and push a grafana panel.

maya: rollout plan: feature-flag server-side stitching (off by default). enable stitching in a small canary org with heavy mobile traffic. watch duplicate-panel and net refunds.
priya: one odd corner: toolcalls that actually truncate prefix (server returns trimmed prefix) — then prefix overlap will be low and stitching won't trigger. we might need a fallback: compare last-k tokens or a short content-hash. bring to reliability review.
alex: noted. i'll add that to the RFC.

josh: TL;DR: cause = reconnect/new-session + no stitch id -> double confirmed stream. fix = stitch-id + billing dedupe + console UX + canary rollout.

maya: sounds good. next: alex please open a ticket with the log snippet + action items, i'll queue UI mock for the console flag. :thumbsup:
alex: done — ticket INF-2114 created. adding owners: @josh, @maya, @priya. thanks all. :pray:
